standard.title: Create informative and imaginative texts
standard.description: create and present informative and imaginative spoken, written and multimodal texts using formulaic expressions, simple phrases and sentences and modelled textual conventions
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can create spoken, written and multimodal texts using familiar words, phrases and modelled language (AC9LS2C05). They have not yet created informative texts for presentation purposes, used modelled textual conventions for specific text types, or created texts for external audiences.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students create and present informative and imaginative spoken, written and multimodal texts using formulaic expressions, simple phrases, sentences and modelled textual conventions across a range of purposes and audiences.

nodes.label: Creating informative texts for presentation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create simple informative texts for presentation — reports, profiles, displays, captions — using familiar vocabulary and modelled sentence structures.
nodes.minimum_width: Create at least one informative text for presentation using at least five target language elements with appropriate content.
nodes.typical_width: Create class reports, visual and digital displays, self-profiles and informative presentations on familiar topics; use captioned photos and digital formats; add labels, captions and descriptions to images; create bilingual texts; describe locations and cultural contexts using modelled language.
wider: Create an informative presentation that goes beyond copying facts — including personal selection of most interesting information and an explanation of why it was chosen
Create a bilingual informative text for a specified audience — making deliberate decisions about which language to use for which part
nodes.hinge_reason: Creating informative texts for presentation introduces the expectation that text creation serves an audience — not only personal expression. Students who cannot produce informative content for a defined purpose and audience cannot engage with the text-type and audience demands of subsequent bands.

response_modes.reason: Informative text creation develops through varied topic and format conditions. Students who only create one type develop narrow production schemas. Varied text types — reports, profiles, displays, maps — build flexible informative production capacity.

success_criteria: Creates an informative text with at least five target language elements appropriate to the topic
Presents the text to an audience using appropriate spoken support

nodes.label: Creating imaginative texts using modelled conventions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create imaginative texts — stories, scripts, adapted performances, songs — using modelled textual conventions and familiar language.
nodes.minimum_width: Create at least one imaginative text using at least one modelled textual convention.
nodes.typical_width: Create puppet shows, adapted stories and fables, alternative versions of songs and rhymes, simple scripts; use modelled narrative conventions; recreate familiar texts for younger audiences; write collaborative imaginative texts with partners.
wider: Create an imaginative text with substantially original content — going beyond substitution to introduce a new character, setting or event
Collaborate with a partner to write an imaginative text where each partner contributes different elements

response_modes.reason: Imaginative text creation develops through varied text types and creative contexts. Creating across story, song, script and performance builds flexible imaginative production capacity.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Imaginative text creation is where students begin to have genuine creative agency in the target language — building the creative confidence that sustains engagement beyond routine tasks.
success_criteria: Creates an imaginative text using at least one modelled textual convention correctly
The text is recognisably imaginative — it has at least one narrative, character or creative element

nodes.label: Presenting texts for genuine audiences
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can present informative and imaginative texts to genuine audiences — using appropriate delivery strategies for the audience and purpose.
nodes.minimum_width: Present at least one text to a real audience using at least one deliberate delivery strategy.
nodes.typical_width: Present texts to varied audiences — class, buddy class, younger learners, assembly; adapt presentation for audience level; use voice, gesture, visual support and props; perform scripts and collaborative productions for real audiences.
wider: Present a text to an audience outside the immediate class — reflecting on what was adapted for that specific audience
Create and deliver a text for a target language community context — making deliberate bilingual decisions about what to present in each language

response_modes.reason: Presentation integrates all prior text creation — informative (N1) and imaginative (N2) — and deploys it for a real communicative purpose. The genuine audience condition is the integration test.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Presenting for genuine audiences gives target language use real communicative purpose and stakes. Students who have presented to real audiences understand the target language is for communication, not only classroom tasks.
success_criteria: Presents a text to a real audience using at least one deliberate delivery strategy
The presentation communicates its intended meaning to the audience
